# UniWALM

UniWALM: Unified World Action Language Model for Embodied Robot Control

**2026-10-20 · Preprint · Brown University**

**[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28626)** · [Project](https://rahulsajnani.github.io/projects/uniwalm/)

A shared diffusion model co-generates video, actions and language memory, with corrective flow training for action deviations.

<img src="../../../website/public/images/catalog/uniwalm-policy.webp" width="760" alt="Figure 2: Overview of UniWALM . UniWALM is a unified mixture-of-transformers (MoT) world-action-language model that co-denoises video, language, and action in a single shared representation. Given the current observation, task instruction, proprioception, an optional visual memory ℱ \mathcal{F} (one or more frames; in our experiments a single anchor at episode start), and the previously generated textual memory , UniWALM processes inputs through a (a) video , (b) language , and (c) action DiT th"/>

**Scope and qualifications**

- Language generation is learned jointly with actions, not evidence of an independent coding-agent harness.
- This work uses RGB deployment observations; no measured-depth claim is established.
